data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's decorrelation test conflates the causal structure of the checklist with the panel's understanding of it. If the checklist explicitly encodes surface cues and the panel merely complies, panel performance on decorrelated items could still survive—not because the checklist encodes causal structure, but because the panel happens to apply unstated background knowledge or an alternative heuristic. The overturn condition acknowledges this ("the panel uses unstated external knowledge"), but then the core claim that survival demonstrates the checklist encodes causal structure is invalid: survival only shows the panel has a reliable pathway, not that the checklist's theory is causal. This fails to distinguish checklist-causal-structure from panel-causal-structure as the source of reliability, which is precisely the distinction the problem asks the single evaluation to make.
